players.product: Neoverse V2/V3 CPU core IP and CSS compute subsystems

quarterly_data.signal: Arm's U.K. Annual Report for the year ended 31 March 2026 (furnished on Form 6-K): the number of extant Arm Total Access licences was 56 at 31 March 2026 (2025: 44) and extant Arm Flexible Access licences 329 (2025: 314). Arm attributes the year's strong demand for its technology primarily to new products introduced in recent years, its licensing model, customers' increased R&D intensity as they develop AI-enabled chips, increased deployments of Arm-based chips in data centres and new high-value licence agreements.
quarterly_data.figure: 56 Arm Total Access licences (2025: 44); 329 Arm Flexible Access licences (2025: 314)

quarterly_data.signal: Arm's U.K. Annual Report for the year ended 31 March 2026 (furnished on Form 6-K): cumulatively, Arm's customers have now shipped more than 350 billion Arm-based chips, and Arm's CPUs enabled advanced computing in greater than 99% of the world's smartphones sold in the fiscal year ended 31 March 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 350 billion Arm-based chips shipped cumulatively; greater than 99% of smartphones sold in FYE26
